subject.title: fix(agents): tighten lsSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally diverge from the upstream Pi tool contract and make count-like built-in tool parameters, beginning with `ls.limit`, schema-level integers?
rationale: Both number acceptance and strict integer rejection are technically viable; choosing the permanent tool-call compatibility policy and whether it must be applied consistently across sibling tools requires owner intent.

options.title: Approve consistent integer schemas
options.body: Confirm count-like parameters are integer-only and coordinate this PR with the related `grep`, `find`, and bash-tool schema changes plus focused compatibility proof.

options.title: Preserve upstream number semantics
options.body: Keep `Type.Number` and retain runtime handling of fractional model output rather than introducing stricter schema rejection.

options.title: Accept an ls-only divergence
options.body: Merge this narrow change while explicitly accepting temporarily inconsistent numeric contracts across built-in tools.

recommendation.title: Approve consistent integer schemas
recommendation.body: Confirm count-like parameters are integer-only and coordinate this PR with the related `grep`, `find`, and bash-tool schema changes plus focused compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The documented Agents ownership area most directly covers the built-in agent-tool schema contract. ([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?utm_source=openai))
